specialisation: agentic coding — 118B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts with 8B active per token, open weights, 1M-token context, positioned by the vendor against SWE and terminal-agent benchmarks
fit_note: A coding/SWE-specialised model measured on a GENERAL-ASSISTANT workload (QA, retrieval, memory, tool orchestration, structured output, safeguards). A weak cell here is at least as likely to be workload mismatch as framework weakness, and must never be read as the latter without the anchor-set correction.

reasoning_mode.note: The vendor reports its headline numbers with thinking ENABLED, and the gap is large: Terminal-Bench 2.1 70.2 with vs 60.4 without; DeepSWE v1.1 40.4 with vs 16.5 without. The arena calls plain chat/completions and passes no thinking parameter, so it exercises whatever the endpoint's default is — which was never verified. Treat every number from this model as an UNCONTROLLED reasoning-mode condition until that is pinned down.

api_quirks: Rejects response_format.json_schema.strict=false with HTTP 400 while accepting true and null — strict:false is OpenAI's documented default and LangChain's, so this hits some frameworks and not others (see arenas/live/langgraph/modes/structured.py).
Accepts response_format json_schema with HTTP 200 but does NOT enforce it: replies come back missing required properties. Confirmed independently under strict=true.
GET /models returns HTTP 502 (text/html); only chat/completions and /responses are usable.

Free developer tier returned 429 "usage limit exceeded" after 1,348 calls / ~567k tokens mid-board, and had NOT cleared ~1 hour later. Whether that is a spent allowance or a long-window throttle was never established — the key was rotated away before it could be re-tested — so treat it as 'did not clear within the run', which is all that was observed. Contrast Agnes, whose free-tier 429 clears within seconds and only needs a slower -rps.
